sources.title: A Theoretical Analysis of Contrastive Unsupervised Representation Learning
sources.author: Sanjeev Arora, Hrishikesh Khandeparkar, Mikhail Khodak, Orestis Plevrakis, Nikunj Saunshi
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted
sources.read_status: Complete main-paper reading: cached PDF pp. 1–10, including the model, theorems, corollaries, discussion, and experiments. The detailed proofs for the main latent-class bounds are in the separately cached supplement and were read there. Main-paper pp. 1–10 are the full document.
sources.claims_used: A latent-class positive-pair model yields a conditional downstream binary-task bound for the class-mean representation of a contrastive ERM. Theorem 4.1 compares against any representation comparator through contrastive loss, a class-collision factor tau, and finite-sample generalization term; Theorem 4.5 adds non-collision and within-class deviation. Corollary 5.1.1 adds within-class sub-Gaussian concentration and a mean-classifier margin. The paper gives counterexamples to stronger supervised-comparator conclusions and warns collisions can make many negatives harmful.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Latent class c sampled from rho; conditionally independent positives from D_c; negatives from the marginal; bounded representation norm; iid sampled triplets; bounded binary loss and a controlled Rademacher complexity; downstream tasks formed from the same class family. Main bound proof route: Jensen from pairwise loss to class means, vector-contraction/Rademacher generalization, and an algebraic block comparison. Supplement supplies the detailed proofs.
sources.gaps: Theory does not cover general multiclass top-1 performance or arbitrary positive-pair semantics. Practical augmentation pipelines need not satisfy the latent-class model. Keep the guarantee conditional and do not imply universal representation quality.

sources.claims_used: SimCLR defines two stochastic augmentations of an example, a shared encoder and projection head, normalized temperature-scaled cross-entropy, and in-batch negatives. Large batches and augmentation composition affect the reported transfer results; the pre-projection representation outperformed the projection output in the reported linear evaluation.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: No formal transfer theorem. The objective identity follows directly from the stated batch logits and cross-entropy; all representation quality comparisons are ImageNet experiments under the reported augmentations, batch sizes, architecture, optimizer, and compute.
sources.gaps: Benchmark outcomes are not a proof of semantic sufficiency or universal invariance. Augmentation choice can induce shortcuts or erase task-relevant distinctions.

sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted

sources.claims_used: MAE feeds visible image patches to an encoder, uses a small decoder for reconstruction, masks a high fraction (reported default 75%) and computes pixel reconstruction loss on masked patches. The reported ImageNet pretraining and downstream transfer outcomes are empirical.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Algorithmic description and empirical evidence only; no theorem that reconstructing masked pixels recovers semantic features or guarantees transfer.
sources.gaps: Results depend on image domain, masking distribution/ratio, architecture, training budget, optimization, and evaluation protocol. The paper does not establish general semantic identifiability.

sources.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
sources.author: Diederik P. Kingma, Max Welling
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted
sources.read_status: Complete cached PDF pp. 1–9 read.
anchors: §2 variational lower bound and KL identity, pp. 2–4
sources.claims_used: For a normalized latent-variable joint p_theta(x,z), the ELBO plus KL(q_phi(z|x)||p_theta(z|x)) equals log p_theta(x). A pathwise Monte Carlo estimator is available when latent sampling is expressed as a differentiable transform of parameter-independent noise.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: The exact ELBO identity follows by expanding the KL to the true posterior, requiring the relevant densities and expectations to exist and the KL to be well-defined. The pathwise gradient requires differentiability and interchange of derivative and expectation; the paper calls assumptions mild but does not state a full general domination theorem.
sources.gaps: An ELBO optimizer need not recover the true posterior, identify latent variables, or calibrate predictions. Finite Monte Carlo and neural optimization add approximation error; no general training guarantee.

sources.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
sources.author: Ian Goodfellow et al.
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted
sources.read_status: Complete cached PDF pp. 1–9 read.
anchors: §2 minimax framework and optimal discriminator, pp. 2–4
§3 theoretical analysis and JS identity, pp. 4–6
§4 experiments and discussion of neural parameterization, pp. 6–9
sources.claims_used: With unrestricted discriminator, pointwise maximization gives D*_G=p_data/(p_data+p_G) almost everywhere for densities; substituting yields C(G)=-log 4+2 JS(p_data||p_G), with a global distribution optimum at p_G=p_data.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Binary cross-entropy objective, densities relative to a common dominating measure, and an unrestricted discriminator class for the pointwise optimum. The convergence proposition assumes unlimited capacity, an optimal discriminator at each step, and small distribution-space updates.
sources.gaps: The paper explicitly does not prove convergence of finite neural alternating optimization. Ideal global distribution optimum must not be reported as a neural training guarantee.

sources.title: Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks
sources.author: Martin Arjovsky, Soumith Chintala, Léon Bottou
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted
sources.read_status: Theory and proof ranges read: cached PDF pp. 1–8 and 20–25. The remaining pp. 9–19 and 26–32 were not read and are not used for dossier claims.
anchors: §2 W1 primal/dual motivation and continuity, pp. 2–4
§3 WGAN objective, assumptions and gradient, pp. 4–8
Appendix proof of continuity/differentiability results, pp. 20–25
sources.claims_used: The paper uses W1 over a compact metric data space and its 1-Lipschitz dual; proves continuity and a.e. differentiability in generator parameters under its stated locally Lipschitz generator and expected local-Lipschitz assumptions; derives the generator gradient using an ideal optimal critic and parameter regularity.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Compact data support; locally Lipschitz generator in latent and parameter variables with the paper’s integrable local-Lipschitz bound; latent coupling for continuity and bounded convergence; ideal 1-Lipschitz optimal critic for the gradient statement. The W1 duality is invoked rather than proved in full.
sources.gaps: No general convergence theorem for the neural saddle-point algorithm, approximate critics, or mode collapse. The authors call weight clipping a poor Lipschitz enforcement method. Do not generalize the compact-space theorem to arbitrary P1 distributions without a separate proof.

sources.title: Normalizing Flows for Probabilistic Modeling and Inference
sources.author: George Papamakarios, Eric Nalisnick, Danilo Jimenez Rezende, Shakir Mohamed, Balaji Lakshminarayanan
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted
sources.read_status: Selected theory sections read: cached PDF pp. 1–6, 12–15, 31–33, 52–54. Other pages were not read and are not used.
anchors: §4 continuous normalizing flow density ODE, pp. 31–33
sources.claims_used: Equal-dimensional global differentiable bijection with differentiable inverse gives transformed density using the absolute Jacobian determinant; composition adds log-Jacobian terms. A triangular conditional-CDF construction represents positive sufficiently smooth densities under its assumptions. For continuous flows, state-Lipschitz continuous-time vector fields yield unique trajectories and log-density evolves as minus the divergence integral.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Density change is the ordinary Euclidean change-of-variables theorem for a global C1 diffeomorphism. Triangular representation requires everywhere positive target density and differentiable conditional CDFs. Continuous flow uses uniform state-Lipschitz regularity and continuous time dependence for unique solutions plus differentiability sufficient for the Jacobian formula.
sources.gaps: Representational existence is not finite-network approximation or trainability. Full-dimensional smooth density models do not directly represent discrete or singular-manifold laws; continuous-flow numerical integration and adjoint gradients are approximations.

sources.title: Estimation of Non-Normalized Statistical Models by Score Matching
sources.author: Aapo Hyvärinen
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted
sources.read_status: Complete cached PDF pp. 1–15 read.
anchors: §2 score matching and integration-by-parts identity, pp. 3–6
sources.claims_used: The expected squared score error equals the tractable derivative-based objective plus a theta-independent constant when data/model scores are square integrable and the boundary product vanishes. The unknown normalizing constant cancels because the model score is the derivative of log unnormalized density. Under correct specification and identifiability, the population score objective is minimized at the target parameter.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Differentiable data density; differentiable model log unnormalized density; finite score and derivative expectations; boundary decay p_data(x) psi_theta(x)->0 at infinity. Expand the square and integrate the cross term by parts. Identifiability/correct specification are separate from the integration identity.
sources.gaps: The paper’s empirical consistency corollary assumes global empirical optimization; its pointwise LLN proof sketch does not supply uniform convergence/argmin regularity. Do not teach that as a general finite-sample or neural consistency theorem.

sources.author: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted

sources.claims_used: The fixed forward Gaussian chain has a closed-form q(x_t|x_0) and Gaussian posterior q(x_{t-1}|x_t,x_0). The variational objective decomposes into Gaussian KL terms. Noise prediction corresponds to a weighted ELBO term; L_simple drops weights and is not exact likelihood maximization.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Finite discrete Markov Gaussian chain and the specified reverse model; Gaussian conditioning and the standard variational lower-bound identity yield the algebraic terms. Exact identities concern the model objective, not the learned score/network or sample quality.
sources.gaps: Finite networks, chosen T, training and sampling are empirical. The paper reports likelihood limitations; no universal fidelity or sampler-convergence theorem.

sources.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
sources.author: Yang Song, Jascha Sohl-Dickstein, Diederik P. Kingma, Abhishek Kumar, Stefano Ermon, Ben Poole
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted
sources.read_status: Cached PDF pp. 1–5, 13–15, 17–19, and 31–32 read. Other appendices and experimental pages were not read and are not relied on.
anchors: §2 SDE framework and score objective, pp. 2–5
appendix reverse SDE/probability flow material, pp. 13–15
sources.claims_used: The score objective characterizes the marginal score at population optimum under sufficient model/data conditions. With exact score and suitable density evolution, the reverse SDE generates the reverse marginals; the probability-flow ODE has identical one-time marginals and a continuous change-of-density formula. Numerical RK and Hutchinson trace calculations used in experiments are approximations.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Reverse-time SDE theorem is attributed to Anderson; its primary theorem/proof was separately read. Use state-independent scalar diffusion for the familiar score-only drift, or include the general divergence term. Probability-flow identity follows by matching Fokker–Planck and continuity equations under smooth density/vector-field conditions.
sources.gaps: Score estimation error, finite prior time, discretization error, and approximate divergence/trace estimation are not controlled by the ideal equations. “Exact likelihood” refers to exact continuous equations, not numerical computation.

sources.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
sources.author: Yaron Lipman, Ricky T. Q. Chen, Heli Ben-Hamu, Maximilian Nickel, Matt Le
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted

anchors: §2 probability paths and marginal vector field, pp. 2–4
Theorems 1–3 and flow/conditional objective derivations, pp. 4–7
appendix regularity, proofs and Gaussian path detail, pp. 14–16
sources.claims_used: Conditional vector fields average to a marginal field generating the marginal path under regularity. Conditional flow-matching objective differs from marginal flow matching by a parameter-independent constant, hence same parameter gradients under stated positivity/integrability/decay conditions. The paper supplies a closed Gaussian conditional path field; conditional OT does not imply the marginal flow is globally OT.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Differentiation under integral/continuity equation regularity; p_t(x)>0; Fubini and sufficient decay/boundedness of conditional and learned fields and parameter derivatives. The gradient identity follows by expanding the squared objective and conditional expectation. Gaussian optimal coupling applies to the stated Gaussian endpoint setting.
sources.gaps: Training and sample-quality/faster-sampling comparisons are empirical. The general marginal flow need not be an optimal transport map; ODE numerical error remains separate.

sources.title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations

Adjoint sensitivities provide a continuous gradient expression under regularity. The proof uses the local Jacobian determinant/Jacobi formula; actual ODESolve tolerances and backsolve gradients incur numerical error.

sources.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
sources.author: Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun, Kilian Q. Weinberger
sources.extraction: PyMuPDF page text; complete document pages extracted

sources.claims_used: Defines top-label calibration and binned ECE/MCE; explains ECE is a bin-dependent approximation with resolution/estimation concerns, not a proper scoring rule. Scalar temperature on logits preserves argmax and is fitted by validation NLL. Reported calibration improvements are empirical on the tested in-distribution tasks.
sources.hypotheses_and_proof: Argmax invariance follows from preserving order for T>0. Validation fitting requires labeled data representative of the evaluation distribution for intended empirical calibration; no distribution-free finite-sample or shifted-distribution guarantee.
